payload.current_view_rule: Replay the CTL current root and project active bindings whose logical id starts with subject:, subject-edge:, subject-index:, or subject-operation:. Generated wiki pages are views over that projection, not the normative record.
payload.migration_notes: If ctl-meta later defines a generic upstream subject profile, migrate by admitting subject-operation:migrate_to_upstream_profile records or replacement subject revisions. Do not rewrite these seed objects in place.
payload.physical_store: Same ctl-dogfood object store and refs/main current root as claims, graphs, policies, and role bindings; this is not a second CTL store.
payload.purpose: Make project-local subject identities, aliases, edge roles, and append-only correction intent visible to future agents and to an upstream ctl-meta reviewer.
review_warnings_addressed: The lane is physically integrated into ctl-dogfood rather than a separate CTL store.
The ty:ambiguous-hub kind is now represented by an active subject definition.
Yasui and Akbulut source papers are represented as paper subjects with arXiv id and versioned id in external_references.
The SU(2) Lie group and SU(2)_k MTC family have separate seed subjects.
SU(3)_2 and SU(3)_3 are represented as category subjects with explicit warnings about incomplete/nonexistent F/R Yasui evaluations.
The Yasui a=3 D(A4) run is represented as an inconclusive partial-computation cluster, not a completed invariant.
Edges in this seed set are admitted subject-edge records, not informal candidate prose.
The index cites prior proposal logical ids and their current claim CIDs at index creation.
payload.title: Twisted Yetter downstream subject lane v0

upstream_review_contract.downstream_scope: This is a Twisted Yetter research-profile experiment. It is not a CTL Kernel feature and not yet an upstream ResearchCTL specification.
first_reading_path: Read the verifier rules in ctl-dogfood/scripts/verify.py for the accepted local schemas.
Read the admitted proposal notes listed in known_proposal_notes only as design history, not as the active schema.
upstream_review_contract.migration_commitment: Twisted Yetter will consume an upstream design by append-only migration records and replacement subject revisions, preserving old subject ids as historical or redirected handles.
questions_for_upstream: Should subject definitions and edges remain opaque-json plus project verifier, or become a generic ctl-data profile?
Should alias collision handling be a hard verifier failure or a current-view warning with explicit disambiguation objects?
Should subject operations be first-class upstream profiles or downstream conventions?
